title: Invisible repairs
bodyMd:
A museum's workshop books list objects sent for repair, the work performed and the materials used. A researcher initially planned to use the books to compare how often different objects broke. She soon noticed that wooden furniture appeared frequently, while inexpensive woven containers almost never appeared. A letter from a former curator explained that damaged woven containers had usually been replaced without passing through the workshop.

The researcher therefore changed her question. The books could illuminate the museum's choices about which possessions deserved skilled repair, but they could not on their own establish the relative durability of all its possessions. An absent repair entry might mean an object remained intact; it might also mean that the object had been discarded. The archive recorded a decision-making process as well as physical damage.
